headline: Penguins' Ben Kindel back in Pittsburgh after medical emergency
take:
ESPN reports that Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh and recovering from a medical emergency on the team's flight home from Utah earlier this week. The report gives no timeline for his return.

So far this season, Kindel has two goals and two assists in nine games while playing 17.32 minutes a night, a real role for a young forward. His results sit slightly under his chances: his shots and passes have been worth 2.45 expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and he has scored two, so he is 0.45 below that mark. That gap is small and not a sign of a real problem. The team is 4.8 percentage points worse in expected goals share when he plays, which is a modest negative, though nine games is a small sample. For PIT, now 3-6-1, the on-ice picture is less bleak than the record: the Penguins hold 47.9 percent of expected goals overall, and 53 percent at five-on-five. His absence, whenever it comes, would cost the team a regular, not a driver. The data doesn't yet show who would absorb his minutes.
